bools.comment: many DMs handle nearly all game mechanics, concealing die rolls and secretly tracking PC hit points and statistics - but a certain amount of mystery is essential to a good game
bools.name: dchMysteryEssential

bools.comment: the overburdened DM with underoccupied players becomes frustrated while they become bored
bools.name: dchOverburdened

bools.comment: the exact tasks the players can help with depend on your desires, the players' level of maturity, and the type of game you wish to run
bools.name: dchTaskNature

bools.comment: as a rule, the more things you allow the players to do, the more smoothly your game progresses - no DM was ever bored for lack of things to do during a gaming session
bools.name: dchMoreAllowed

bools.comment: tournament play or highly competitive campaigns require more DM supervision; mature and trustworthy PCs may take on many responsibilities of running the game
bools.name: dchSupervision

bools.comment: rolling up player characters is usually fun; with a cooperative party, PC creation should require little or no DM involvement
bools.name: dchRollingFun

bools.comment: players may supervise each other's dice rolls, and you should be sure they understand which PC generation procedure the campaign uses
bools.name: dchRollingProcedure

bools.comment: the time gained at a new campaign's start adds final setting details; in an ongoing campaign the generation time still attends to other details
bools.name: dchRollingTimeGained

bools.comment: new players are briefed by the others on the adventure's circumstances; experienced players teach the classes and races and lead novices through generation, leaving the DM free
bools.name: dchRollingNovices

bools.comment: employing the players' ideas for adventures is a helpful tactic, but it needs thinking ahead at least to the next gaming session
bools.name: dchIdeasThinkAhead

bools.comment: ask between adventures or at a story line's end what type of adventure they would like next; the players suggest the general category, you create the details
bools.name: dchIdeasAskCategory

bools.comment: the drow kingdom example: the preference for a long underground expedition, the route to the vast realms and wealth, the clues leading to the dungeon entrance and the tortuous maze
bools.name: dchIdeasDrowExample

bools.comment: the tactic is handy when adventures fall flat; asking in advance aligns the story with the players' desires
bools.name: dchIdeasInAdvance

bools.comment: player feedback works during the game too - consider adjusting your story to meet the players' expectations as you go along
bools.name: dchIdeasLiveFeedback

bools.comment: characters of different classes may have obligations from game rules or campaign considerations - primarily an area of PC responsibility, with the DM ensuring understanding and the occasional reminder
bools.name: dchClassObligations

bools.comment: the cleric's treasure donation to his deity varies per campaign but is fairly universal; the thief joins the local guild and donates a portion of his gains to its coffers
bools.name: dchClassDonations

bools.comment: the players make the donation calculations and inform you of the amounts - the DM should not record donations at the end of every adventure
bools.name: dchClassBookkeeping

bools.comment: an occasional investigation by the guildmaster or high cleric keeps tabs on the characters, made into an interesting game encounter rather than routine bookkeeping
bools.name: dchClassInvestigations

bools.comment: PCs are responsible for acquiring spellcasting components, deducting the money spent and noting the newly gained components; hard-to-buy components are adjudicated - the druid's quest for greater mistletoe as an interesting short adventure
bools.name: dchClassComponents

bools.comment: players should control their own henchmen and hirelings unless those NPCs are being taken advantage of; the DM may step in and run them at any time, but only when necessary
bools.name: dchHenchmenControl

bools.comment: taking over henchman actions is a technique for imparting information to the players and protecting the NPCs from unusually dangerous situations; otherwise the players handle things well
bools.name: dchHenchmenTakeover

bools.comment: detail these NPCs as much as possible when generated - once a player knows his henchman is selfish and whiny, he portrays that NPC as selfish and whiny
bools.name: dchHenchmenDetail

bools.comment: require players to keep track of NPCs and their usual locations: Olaf of the Black Tooth met at the Shaggy Mammoth Inn is remembered by the players, not the DM
bools.name: dchHenchmenTrack

bools.comment: players aid in stocking the campaign with NPCs: the sought blacksmith assumed to exist with a persona created on the spot; when not necessarily present, assign a probability by community size and NPC availability and roll the dice
bools.name: dchHenchmenStocking
